text:
Arjun: hey all, second day, trying to finish the bootstrap. i'm on an M2 with fish shell and i think my PATH ordering is wrong. installed asdf via brew but `node` and `python` are still pointing to system versions. VSCode integrated terminal also ignores my fish config. any fish-specific tips?
Maya: welcome Arjun! :wave: fish is a bit different from bash/zsh. check `which asdf` and `asdf current` first. fish doesn't read ~/.zshrc so you need to add the asdf fish hook.
Arjun: `which asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf. `asdf current` shows nothing even after install. i ran `asdf plugin-add nodejs` and `asdf install nodejs 20.5.0` but `asdf global nodejs` seems ignored.
Maya: for fish, add to ~/.config/fish/config.fish:
```
# ASDF (homebrew install)
set -gx ASDF_DIR /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf
source $ASDF_DIR/libexec/asdf.fish
function fish_user_key_bindings; and asdf reshim; end
```
Then restart fish (or run `exec fish`). `asdf reshim` after installs.
Omar: also ensure fish_user_paths has brew and ~/.local/bin earlier: `set -U fish_user_paths /opt/homebrew/bin $HOME/.local/bin $fish_user_paths`. fish prepends differently so ordering matters.
Arjun: ok adding that. quick q on pyenv vs asdf python: i have strange pip packages installed globally and venvs don't find them. recommended pattern?
Maya: use asdf for the runtime and then create venvs per project: `asdf install python 3.11.4 && asdf global python 3.11.4` then inside project `python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate`. avoid using `pip install --user` globally.
Arjun: VSCode still doesn't detect the .venv interpreter in a project opened via the repo root. integrated terminal shows correct python though.
Omar: VSCode + fish edge case: the extension host uses your login shell. set VSCode setting `terminal.integrated.shell.osx` to `/opt/homebrew/bin/fish`. also enable `python.terminal.activateEnvironment` true. If you open VSCode via Dock it might not pick up your login env — open from terminal with `code .` after `exec fish`.
Arjun: got it. what about dotfiles? i cloned the internal dotfiles but the symlink script fails on a permission error for ~/.ssh/config.
Maya: probably because the script tries to chown. run the symlink script with `./scripts/dev-setup` but don't sudo. If it complains about existing file, move the old config `mv ~/.ssh/config ~/.ssh/config.backup` then re-run. ssh config should set `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and `AddKeysToAgent yes`.
Arjun: ssh agent still asks for passphrase each push even after adding to keychain. I'm using macOS ssh agent managed by Keychain.
Omar: use `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and ensure `Host github.com` block in ~/.ssh/config includes `UseKeychain yes`. then restart the agent: `killall ssh-agent` (it will respawn) and `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
Arjun: thanks. last thing: REDWOOD_* env vars. quickstart mentions REDWOOD_API_URL and REDWOOD_API_KEY. where should i store them locally?
Maya: put secrets in `.env.local` (added to .gitignore). we keep canonical placeholders in `.env.example`. for secrets we use 1Password teams: `op item get "redwood/dev/api-key" --fields label=password` if you have 1p access.
